title: The upper n-density ratio limsup of an arbitrary measure is Borel measurable (supplied proof, step 1)
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let μ be any measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra). For x ∈ ℝ^P let Θ*(x) := limsup_{ρ→0⁺} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n), the limsup taken in [0, ∞] along the filter 𝓝[>]0, where B_ρ(x) is the open ball and ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^n (the quotient is ENNReal division by ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)). Then x ↦ Θ*(x).toReal is Borel measurable on ℝ^P. No finiteness assumption on μ is made.
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), Measurable (fun x : Euclid P => (limsup (fun ρ : ℝ => μ (ball x ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0)).toReal)
